key_insight: Strong internal stroke-classification performance did not generalize: F1 fell from 95.48% internally to approximately 58–62% in multicenter external validation.
clinical_relevance: Low ischemic-stroke sensitivity and a tendency to overdiagnose hemorrhage raise concerns about reliability in acute stroke triage.
method: Three-channel CT preprocessing used radiological Hounsfield Unit windows and asymmetric .mat/.png formats.
CNN and Vision Transformer features were combined through cross-attention fusion with Integrated Orthogonal-Focal Loss.
External evaluation used a Mask Anchor filter, while multi-seed analysis assessed model stability.
evidence_signal: External testing on AISD, BHSD, and PhysioNet showed ischemic-stroke precision of 77% but sensitivity of 57%; DenseNet201+ViT had the lowest reported multi-seed deviation (0.59).
watch_item: Low variability across seeds does not establish clinical readiness, especially given the large external-performance drop and missed ischemic strokes.
paper_title: Acute Stroke Classification Using Asymmetric Data Standardization and Orthogonal-Focal Loss Optimized CNN-ViT Cross-Attention Fusion: A Multicenter External Validation Study
